review_notes: Read all 175 lines of Mathlib/Control/Traversable/Equiv.lean and inspected the relevant surrounding API in Mathlib/Control/Traversable/Basic.lean (the LawfulTraversable fields id_traverse, comp_traverse, traverse_eq_map_id, naturality) and Mathlib/Control/Traversable/Lemmas.lean (traverse lemmas and the functor_norm attribute). I considered the uniform 'conjugate by eqv / eqv.symm' structure shared by Equiv.map and Equiv.traverse and by the proofs of id_map, comp_map, id_traverse, traverse_eq_map_id, comp_traverse and naturality. Each of those proofs is a one-line simp/rw that unfolds the transfer definition, applies a different underlying law of t, and cancels symm_apply_apply/apply_symm_apply; there is no common nontrivial sub-argument worth extracting, and any shared helper would be a thin unfolding wrapper. I also considered lawfulFunctor' and isLawfulTraversable', which both transport lawfulness from an arbitrary instance satisfying equality hypotheses, but their arguments are genuinely different: lawfulFunctor' replaces the Functor record by cases/extensionality, while isLawfulTraversable' constructs the LawfulTraversable fields and its source comment explains that the record-replacement approach cannot be reused because h₂ requires a LawfulApplicative parameter. The repeated rw [h₂, ..., h₂] lines in the latter are separate field boilerplate, not repeated mathematical reasoning. No finding satisfies the 'repeated nontrivial proof machinery' bar.
